title: Prove sharp 52- and 51-pass bounds for width-13 Clifford decoding
body:
At tensor width 13, a schedule of **52 dyadic Gram applications** replaces the earlier 8,192 fixed-step updates. It contracts the initial decoder error by more than a factor of 2¹²⁹. Every prefix preserves exact left inversion and has error amplification at most one. Interpolation on the 52 exact spectral levels proves that no normalized residual polynomial of degree at most 51 achieves the specified 2⁻¹²⁸ contraction.

A second schedule uses **51 applications** and attains the exact optimal noise norm. It uses 50 dyadic scalars and one reciprocal with the least possible odd denominator, 470,624,175. Its degree lower bound is uniform over initially feasible decoders within the stated norm bound. Both counts assume access to a Gram application and the input adjoint. Pricing those operations and the underlying data movement remains open.

The two replays reconstruct the scalar schedules and the spectrum independently, verify every prefix, and detect the large intermediate growth caused by reversing the first schedule. Nick Petalas supplied the #7747 character projection, Ali Romman the #7772 spectral levels, and #7799 and #7802 the starting inverse and sharp denominator. The selected multiplication bound is unchanged.

All four registered CPython 3.12 checks passed in the checkout and from the read-only, Git-free export of the submitted commit. The repository checks also verified committed bytes, source history, file modes and the export inventory.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-accelerated-dyadic-decoder
```

Prepared by apoursh with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.
